walkthroughs.body_html:
Tests for Ions & Gases — a core area of GCSE Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Tests for Ions & Gases brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Tests for Ions & Gases.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Sodium has atomic number 11. Its electron configuration is:
An atom of Mg loses 2 electrons to form Mg²⁺. Its number of protons is:
What is the difference between a strong acid and a concentrated acid?
options: The number of peaks equals the total number of protons in the molecule.
A strong acid is one that has been heated to higher temperature.
Strong and concentrated mean the same thing for acids.
A strong acid fully dissociates in water; a concentrated acid has a high amount of acid per volume — these are independent properties.

mcqs.q: In 1H NMR, what does the n+1 rule predict?
options: The number of peaks equals the total number of protons in the molecule.
Splitting tells you how many protons are in the same chemical environment as the one giving the peak.
A proton with n equivalent neighbouring protons will appear as a peak split into n+1 sub-peaks.
The system shifts to amplify the change because reactions always proceed in the disturbed direction.

mcqs.q: When a stress shifts an equilibrium, does the system fully undo the change?
options: The system shifts to amplify the change because reactions always proceed in the disturbed direction.
No — Le Chatelier's principle says the system PARTIALLY opposes the change; equilibrium shifts to a new position that minimises but doesn't eliminate the disturbance.
The system shifts to completely cancel the change and return concentrations to their original values.
The number of peaks equals the total number of protons in the molecule.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Ion”?
options: Number of protons in the nucleus; defines the element.
Atom or group of atoms with an overall charge from losing or gaining electrons.
Average mass of atoms of an element compared to 1/12 the mass of a C-12 atom.
Arrangement of electrons in shells: 2, 8, 8 for the first three shells.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Mass number”?
options: Total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.
Average mass of atoms of an element compared to 1/12 the mass of a C-12 atom.
Atom or group of atoms with an overall charge from losing or gaining electrons.
Number of protons in the nucleus; defines the element.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Atom”?
options: Atom or group of atoms with an overall charge from losing or gaining electrons.
Arrangement of electrons in shells: 2, 8, 8 for the first three shells.
Total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.
Smallest unit of an element; consists of a nucleus of protons and neutrons surrounded by electrons.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Relative atomic mass”?

Average mass of atoms of an element compared to 1/12 the mass of a C-12 atom.
Arrangement of electrons in shells: 2, 8, 8 for the first three shells.
Atom or group of atoms with an overall charge from losing or gaining electrons.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Atomic number”?
